elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once in any rolling 12-month period.
elements.evidence: The clause limits inspections to once “per year,” which may mean a calendar or contract year and does not clearly prevent inspections less than 12 months apart.

elements.element: Customer must receive at least 30 days' prior written notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires “no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company.”

elements.element: Audits must be conducted during Customer's normal business hours.
elements.evidence: Inspection is expressly limited to “the Company's normal business hours.”

elements.element: The audit must be conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The inspection right is granted to HDI's General Manager, not to an independent auditor.

elements.element: The auditor must be bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: The operative clause imposes no confidentiality obligation on the person conducting the inspection.

elements.element: Vendor must bear the audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5%.
elements.evidence: The clause requires HDI to bear its inspection fees in all cases, which is at least as protective of Customer as permitting cost-shifting only when underpayment exceeds 5%.

elements.element: The audit right must not permit direct access to Customer systems.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no prohibition on direct systems access, and the right to inspect records could encompass electronically maintained records.

elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly limits inspection to “no more than once per year.”

elements.element: Customer must receive at least 15 days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires at least 30 days' prior written notice, exceeding the 15-day fallback requirement.

elements.element: Vendor must bear the audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10%.
elements.evidence: The clause requires HDI to bear its inspection fees in all cases, which is more protective of Customer than allowing cost-shifting when underpayment exceeds 10%.

result.reason: The redline minimally adds the frequency restriction needed to complete the fallback while retaining the existing notice, business-hours, scope, and cost provisions. It does not satisfy the preferred position because “once per year” is not clearly a rolling 12-month limit, the inspector is HDI's General Manager rather than an independent confidential auditor, and there is no express prohibition on direct systems access. The drafting is understandable but retains awkward phrasing such as “may ... have the right” and uses the potentially ambiguous “per year” formulation.
